content:
Solve the equivalent system:
\[
23b+15c\equiv 2-a \pmod{26},\qquad 11b+10c\equiv 4\pmod{26}.
\]
The second congruence comes from subtracting twice the first equation from the second.

From the first minus twice the second:
\[
b-5c\equiv -a-6 \pmod{26},
\]
so
\[
b\equiv 5c-a-6 \pmod{26}.
\]
Substitute into \(11b+10c\equiv 4\):
\[
11(5c-a-6)+10c\equiv 4 \pmod{26}
\]
\[
65c-11a-66\equiv 4 \pmod{26}
\]
\[
13c-11a+12\equiv 4 \pmod{26}
\]
\[
13c\equiv 11a-8 \pmod{26}.
\]
Since \(13c\pmod{26}\) is only \(0\) or \(13\), we need
\[
11a-8\equiv 0 \text{ or } 13 \pmod{26}.
\]
Thus
\[
11a\equiv 8 \pmod{26}
\quad\text{or}\quad
11a\equiv 21 \pmod{26}.
\]
Since \(11^{-1}\equiv 19\pmod{26}\),
\[
a\equiv 8\cdot 19\equiv 22 \pmod{26}
\]
or
\[
a\equiv 21\cdot 19\equiv 9 \pmod{26}.
\]
For \(1\le a\le 26\), the valid values are \(a=9,22\). Their sum is
\[
9+22=31.
\]
\[
\boxed{31}
\]
